Hospital course:
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted for screening mammography x-ray which showed a nodule of about 2 cm against the external quadrant of the right breast. The patient underwent a quadrantectomy of the right breast with removal of 2 cm neoplastic nodule and three ipsilateral sentinel lymph nodes. Follow-up tests showed a moderately differentiated invasive ductal carcinoma containing osteoclast-like giant cells. The patient was treated with adjuvant chemotherapy and hormone therapy with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analogue and exemestane. The patient will also undergo radiotherapy treatment on the residual breast after chemotherapy.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Adjuvant chemotherapy with Docetaxel-Cyclophosphamide q21 scheme for 4 cycles followed by hormone therapy with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analogue and exemestane.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient should continue with hormone therapy and attend follow-up appointments to monitor their condition. Patients should be aware of the benefits and risks related to the therapeutic proposals and follow the instructions as prescribed.

text:
## Principal diagnosis: **C50.9 – Malignant neoplasm of breast, unspecified** (right breast)

This assumes the record doesn't specify the quadrant any further.

### Rationale
- **Condition:** The patient was admitted with a 2 cm right breast nodule. Histology after quadrantectomy confirmed a **moderately differentiated invasive ductal carcinoma with osteoclast-like giant cells**. This is a primary malignant neoplasm of the breast, so it belongs in category **C50**.
- **Subsite:** The summary says only the "external quadrant," which means outer or lateral. It doesn't say upper or lower, so neither of these codes can be assigned:
  - C50.4 Upper-outer quadrant
  - C50.5 Lower-outer quadrant
  
  Without further documentation, the default is **C50.9**.
- **Morphology code:** M8500/3 (infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS), grade 2 (moderately differentiated). The osteoclast-like giant cell feature is a rare variant but doesn't change the ductal carcinoma morphology code.

### Coding notes
- **Query the clinician or check the radiology and pathology reports for laterality detail.** If the lesion is documented as upper-outer, code **C50.4**. If lower-outer, code **C50.5**. Upper-outer is the most common site, but it shouldn't be assumed.
- **Lymph nodes:** Three sentinel nodes were removed, but their status isn't reported. Don't assign C77.3 (secondary malignancy of axillary lymph nodes) unless metastasis is documented.
- **If the episode were an admission specifically for chemotherapy,** the principal diagnosis would be **Z51.1** (Pharmacotherapy session for neoplasm), with C50.x as an additional diagnosis. This summary describes the surgical episode, so **C50.x is principal**.
